question: Does standard M-theory canon REQUIRE Planck-uniform compactification of 7D across 4D spacetime?
evidence_a: Wikipedia M-theory primary text: 7D 'compactified' at scales 'sufficiently small to escape detection'; no explicit position-dependence statement
evidence_b: Wikipedia KK primary text: standard KK treats radius as uniform global constant; ORIGINAL Kaluza permitted Lambda = g_55 to vary fiber-to-fiber; Wesson space-time-matter variant drops cylinder condition
evidence_c: Wikipedia Randall-Sundrum: warping ALONG fifth dimension only, NOT across observable 3D; rc constant; warping factor fixed geometric property
evidence_d: Acharya-Witten 2001 abstract: 'M-theory compactification on a manifold X of G_2 holonomy can give chiral fermions in four dimensions only if X is singular' — describes compactification on a single manifold X with conical singularities; does not specify position-dependence of overall 7D size
verdict_note: Standard M-theory CANON is canonically PRESENTED as Planck-uniform, but no theorem in the surveyed primary sources strictly FORBIDS body-localized + d_geom-scaled variation; the original Kaluza variant explicitly permits fiber-to-fiber variation of the compactification parameter; AW 2001 is silent on the question (its concern is singularity structure of a single X, not how X varies with body-location); RS model has fixed rc but along-extra-dim warping shows the canon ACCOMMODATES non-trivial position-dependence in the geometry

implication: Framework's body-localized + d_geom-scaled compactification reframe candidate is NOT FORBIDDEN by surveyed M-theory canon, but IS NOT STANDARD; it sits in the same conceptual family as Kaluza's original fiber-varying Lambda and as RS warped extra-dim geometry, neither of which is the modern textbook framing
